appraisal_events.evidence: Le mot d'Oriane fait vivre les salons pendant une semaine («le mot se mangeait encore froid le lendemain à déjeuner… et repassait sous diverses sauces pendant la semaine»); les Courvoisier «n'étaient pas davantage capables de s'élever jusqu'à l'esprit d'innovation que la duchesse de Guermantes introduisait dans la vie mondaine», qui «en faisait quelque chose d'artistique»; là où la Courvoisier ne sait qu'appliquer des règles rigides, la duchesse réunit pour la princesse Mathilde «le plus riche bouquet de toutes les beautés, de toutes les valeurs, de toutes les célébrités», et la princesse l'embrasse en l'assurant «qu'elle n'avait jamais passé une meilleure journée».
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage's dominant movement is a sustained elevation of the duchesse: her wit circulates as the salon's prized currency, and the narrator's own comparison with the Courvoisiers credits her with instinct, art, and social invention, capped by an imperial guest's warm endorsement.

appraisal_events.evidence: Elle écarquille les yeux «par une admiration a priori» qui réclame des explications, reprend le mot «rédaction» «qu'elle n'eût pas su appliquer toute seule»; Mme d'Épinay la traite de «pareille dinde»; le narrateur invoque «la culture infiniment arriérée de la princesse», stupéfiée par des paradoxes de seconde main sur Flaubert ou Wagner, et incapable de «séparer le véritable esprit des Guermantes des formes rudimentairement apprises de cet esprit».
appraisal_events.explanation: The princesse de Parme is steadily lowered as the comic measure of Guermantes wit: she admires without understanding, borrows formulas she cannot use, and is explicitly mocked both by the princesse d'Épinay and by the narrator's account of her backwardness.

status_effects.explanation: Her visits and her mot are treated as events one is desolate to have missed; she is deferred to across salons and receives an imperial guest more successfully than any Courvoisier could.

Her verbal authority governs the whole passage — her expressions are imitated and her judgments settle reputations — but the closing narratorial verdict on her critical sterility keeps this short of a maximal gain.
She is presented as slow, backward, and dependent on borrowed formulas, and is called a goose behind her back; her rank is untouched but her local standing as a mind is plainly lowered.

They lose comparatively: their rigid geometry of invitation and their inability to rise to Guermantes wit are the foil against which the duchesse's superiority is measured, and their self-defence about lineage is left sounding hollow.

ambiguities: The narrator both endorses the duchesse's superiority over the Courvoisiers (her «sûr instinct», her «esprit d'innovation», her art of receiving) and, in the closing development, deflates her — «Mme de Guermantes était elle-même beaucoup moins avancée qu'elle ne le croyait», her mondaine wit being to real activity «ce qu'est en art la critique à la création». E1 is scored as elevation because the passage's dominant body stages her social and inventive ascendancy, but that late qualification materially tempers the reading and is the reason her rhetorical gain is only +1.

The elevation of Oriane is delivered largely through irony aimed at her worshippers rather than through direct praise: the mot is «mangé froid le lendemain» and «repassait sous diverses sauces», and the princesse d'Épinay, who has «la prétention d'avoir assimilé l'esprit des Guermantes», uses the borrowed word «rédaction» «sans beaucoup de discernement» while calling Oriane snobbish. That real diminishment of d'Épinay is subordinate to the two dominant movements and is deliberately not recorded as a third event.
